subjective: Marty is a 16-year-old Indie dog with difficulty standing steadily due to hind leg weakness. He is very active during the night from midnight to 6 a.m., roaming around the house, which disturbs the household. Marty attempts to get up to drink water or milk. The owner reports that Marty drops food when it is placed at a height, so they are considering placing food on the ground again for easier access. The owner is concerned about joint pain and is seeking options beyond comfort care to improve muscle structure in the back.
objective: Only one X-ray has been performed. No blood tests were taken during this consultation. Physical examination findings include hind limb weakness with difficulty standing steadily, requiring wall support. No other objective data such as vital signs or additional diagnostics were provided.
assessment: Marty is an elderly dog exhibiting hind limb weakness and joint pain, resulting in instability when standing. The limited diagnostic workup includes a single X-ray. The clinical signs suggest musculoskeletal issues likely related to age, with possible muscle weakness and joint discomfort. The owner is seeking therapeutic options to improve muscle structure and comfort.
plan: Continue with the current supplements as per the dosing schedule, with the second dose administered and consideration for the fourth dose after one week based on condition. No blood tests are planned at this time to avoid stress. Adjust feeding arrangements by placing food and water bowls on the ground to facilitate easier access. Monitor Marty’s mobility and comfort, and consider further diagnostics or therapeutic interventions if condition worsens or does not improve.
conclusion: Marty, a 16-year-old Indie dog, presents with hind limb weakness and joint pain causing difficulty standing steadily. The owner reports nocturnal activity and challenges with feeding arrangements. A single X-ray has been performed, and no blood tests were done during this consultation. The current management includes supplements with a planned dosing schedule. Feeding bowls will be repositioned to ground level to aid feeding. The owner is seeking options to improve muscle structure and comfort. Continued monitoring and reassessment are advised.
